STEP 1: Load and Clean Observational Data

```{r}
# ---- STEP 1: Load and Clean N2O Observational Data ----
# Load Excel file
df <- read_excel("Data_N2O_Guided Research_Shaivan_v1.xlsx")

# Clean decimal format
df <- df %>%
  mutate(`N2O Emission (μmol N₂O m⁻² d⁻¹)` = gsub(",", ".", `N2O Emission (μmol N₂O m⁻² d⁻¹)`))

# Rename and clean up columns
df_clean <- df %>%
  rename(lat = `Latitude (°)`,
         lon = `Longitude (°)`,
         flux_raw = `N2O Emission (μmol N₂O m⁻² d⁻¹)`,
         type = `Point or Region`) %>%
  mutate(
    lat = as.numeric(lat),
    lon = as.numeric(lon),
    flux = flux_raw %>%
      as.character() %>%
      str_replace_all("\u00A0", "") %>%
      str_replace_all("−", "-") %>%
      str_replace_all(",", ".") %>%
      str_trim() %>%
      as.numeric()
  )

# Keep only valid point observations
df_points <- df_clean %>%
  filter(type == "Point", !is.na(lat), !is.na(lon), !is.na(flux))

# Summary
summary(df_points$flux)
```

```{r}
# ---- STEP 2: Extract Environmental Predictors from NetCDF ----
# Setup spatial points for extraction
# Convert sampling coordinates to terra SpatVector
coords_vect <- vect(df_points, geom = c("lon", "lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")

# ---- Helper function: extract surface variable from NetCDF ----
extract_var <- function(nc_file, varname, label, df) {
  r <- rast(nc_file, subds = varname)
  # Assign CRS explicitly to avoid transformation warnings
  crs(r) <- "EPSG:4326"
  surface <- r[[grep("depth=0", names(r))]]
  vals <- terra::extract(surface, coords_vect)[, 2]
  df[[label]] <- vals
  return(df)
}

# ---- Extract WOA environmental variables ----
df_points <- extract_var("woa2023_Nitrate.nc",    "n_an", "nitrate",     df_points)
df_points <- extract_var("woa2023_Phosphate.nc",  "p_an", "phosphate",   df_points)
df_points <- extract_var("woa2023_DisOxygen.nc",  "o_an", "oxygen",      df_points)
df_points <- extract_var("woa2023_Salinity.nc",   "s_an", "salinity",    df_points)
df_points <- extract_var("woa2023_Temperature.nc","t_an","temperature",  df_points)
df_points <- extract_var("woa2018_Density.nc",    "I_an", "density",     df_points)

# ---- Bathymetry (depth) ----
bathy_raster <- rast("GEBCO_2025_sub_ice.nc")
df_points$depth <- terra::extract(bathy_raster, coords_vect)[, 2]

# ---- Chlorophyll (Copernicus, surface only) ----
chl_file1 <- "cmems_mod_glo_bgc_my_0.25deg_P1M-m_1760291720536.nc"      # 1993–2022
chl_file2 <- "cmems_mod_glo_bgc_myint_0.25deg_P1M-m_1760291822771.nc"   # 2023–2025
r1 <- rast(chl_file1)
r2 <- rast(chl_file2)

surface_names_r1 <- grep("chl_depth=0.50576", names(r1), value = TRUE)
surface_names_r2 <- grep("chl_depth=0.50576", names(r2), value = TRUE)

chl_stack1 <- r1[[surface_names_r1]]
chl_stack2 <- r2[[surface_names_r2]]
chl_full_stack <- c(chl_stack1, chl_stack2)
chlorophyll_r <- mean(chl_full_stack, na.rm = TRUE)

df_points$chlorophyll <- terra::extract(chlorophyll_r, coords_vect)[, 2]
```

```{r}
# STEP 3: Prepare dataset for modeling
predictor_vars <- c("temperature", "salinity", "oxygen", "nitrate",
                    "phosphate", "chlorophyll", "density", "depth")
target_var <- "flux"

# Keep complete rows only
df_model <- df_points %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(c(target_var, predictor_vars))) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.))

# Summary check
print(nrow(df_model))
summary(df_model)
```

```{r}
# STEP 4: Split into Training and Test Sets
set.seed(42)
train_indices <- sample(seq_len(nrow(df_model)), size = 0.8 * nrow(df_model))
train_data <- df_model[train_indices, ]
test_data  <- df_model[-train_indices, ]
```

```{r}
# STEP 5: Train Random Forest Model
# ================================================================
rf_model <- randomForest(
  flux ~ .,
  data = train_data,
  ntree = 500,
  importance = TRUE
)

print(rf_model)
varImpPlot(rf_model)

# Evaluate performance on test set
pred_test <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_data)
cat("Test RMSE:", sqrt(mean((pred_test - test_data$flux)^2)), "\n")
cat("Test R²:", cor(pred_test, test_data$flux)^2, "\n")

# Plot observed vs predicted
ggplot(data.frame(obs = test_data$flux, pred = pred_test),
       aes(x = obs, y = pred)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "darkgreen") +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Observed Flux", y = "Predicted Flux",
       title = "Random Forest N2O Flux Prediction") +
  theme_minimal()

```

10-Fold Cross Validation

```{r}
# ----  Train Random Forest Model with 10-fold Cross-Validation ----
set.seed(42)

# Define 10-fold CV setup
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 10,
  verboseIter = TRUE,
  savePredictions = "final"
)

# Define tuning grid for mtry (number of variables tried at each split)
rf_grid <- expand.grid(mtry = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10))

# Run cross-validated training
rf_cv <- train(
  flux ~ .,
  data = df_model,
  method = "rf",
  trControl = ctrl,
  tuneGrid = rf_grid,
  ntree = 500,
  importance = TRUE
)

print(rf_cv)
plot(rf_cv)

# Extract best parameters and performance
best_mtry <- rf_cv$bestTune$mtry
mean_R2   <- rf_cv$results$Rsquared[rf_cv$results$mtry == best_mtry]
mean_RMSE <- rf_cv$results$RMSE[rf_cv$results$mtry == best_mtry]
cat("Best mtry:", best_mtry, "\n")
cat("10-fold CV mean R²:", round(mean_R2, 3), "\n")
cat("10-fold CV mean RMSE:", round(mean_RMSE, 3), "\n")

# ---- Retrain final Random Forest model using full dataset and best mtry ----
rf_final <- randomForest(
  flux ~ .,
  data = df_model,
  ntree = 500,
  mtry = best_mtry,
  importance = TRUE
)

saveRDS(rf_final, "rf_final_model.rds")

# Variable importance
varImpPlot(rf_final, main = "Variable Importance (10-fold RF Model)")
```

```{r}
# ---- STEP 6: Evaluate Final 10-fold CV Model ----
# Predict using final model (trained on full dataset)
pred_final <- predict(rf_final, newdata = df_model)

# Compute performance metrics (approximation on full data)
r_squared_final <- cor(pred_final, df_model$flux)^2
rmse_final <- sqrt(mean((pred_final - df_model$flux)^2))

cat("Final RF Model R² (approx.):", round(r_squared_final, 3), "\n")
cat("Final RF Model RMSE (approx.):", round(rmse_final, 3), "\n")
cat("Cross-validated R² (10-fold mean):", round(mean_R2, 3), "\n")
cat("Cross-validated RMSE (10-fold mean):", round(mean_RMSE, 3), "\n")
```


```{r}
# ---- STEP 8: Add Coordinates as Predictors ----
# Extract lon/lat back from spatial object
coords <- crds(coords_vect)

df_points$lon <- coords[, 1]
df_points$lat <- coords[, 2]
```

```{r}
# ---- STEP 9: Add Log-transformed Flux ----
df_points <- df_points %>%
  mutate(log_flux = log(flux + 1e-3))  # Add epsilon to avoid log(0)

# ---- STEP 10: Prepare Enhanced Modelling Dataset ----
predictor_vars_extended <- c("temperature", "salinity", "oxygen", "nitrate", 
                             "phosphate", "chlorophyll", "density", "depth", 
                             "lat", "lon")
target_var_log <- "log_flux"

# Only keep complete cases
model_data_extended <- df_points %>%
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(target_var_log, predictor_vars_extended))) %>%
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.)))
```

```{r}
# ================================================================
# ---- STEP 11–13: Secondary Manual Train/Test RF (for comparison) ----
# ================================================================

# ---- STEP 11: Split into Training and Test Sets (80/20) ----
set.seed(123)
train_indices_log <- sample(seq_len(nrow(model_data_extended)), size = 0.8 * nrow(model_data_extended))
train_data_log <- model_data_extended[train_indices_log, ]
test_data_log  <- model_data_extended[-train_indices_log, ]

# ---- STEP 12: Train Random Forest on Log-Flux ----
rf_log <- randomForest(
  log_flux ~ ., 
  data = train_data_log, 
  ntree = 500,
  importance = TRUE
)

# ---- STEP 13: Evaluate Log-Flux Model ----
pred_log_flux_log <- predict(rf_log, newdata = test_data_log)
pred_flux_log <- exp(pred_log_flux_log)  # Back-transform

# Compare to actual (non-log) flux
actual_flux_log <- exp(test_data_log$log_flux)

r_squared_log <- cor(pred_flux_log, actual_flux_log)^2
rmse_log <- sqrt(mean((pred_flux_log - actual_flux_log)^2))
mae_log <- mean(abs(pred_flux_log - actual_flux_log))
bias_log <- mean(pred_flux_log - actual_flux_log)

# Calibration slope (regression)
cal_model_log <- lm(actual_flux_log ~ pred_flux_log)
slope_log <- coef(cal_model_log)[2]

cat("\n===== Manual 80/20 RF Model (log-transformed) =====\n")
cat("Test R²:", round(r_squared_log, 3), "\n")
cat("Test RMSE:", round(rmse_log, 3), "\n")
cat("MAE:", round(mae_log, 3), "\n")
cat("Bias:", round(bias_log, 3), "\n")
cat("Calibration Slope:", round(slope_log, 3), "\n")

# ---- Optional: Visualize Performance ----
varImpPlot(rf_log, main = "Variable Importance (RF, log-transformed 80/20 Model)")

plot(actual_flux_log, pred_flux_log,
     xlab = "Observed Flux (µmol m⁻² d⁻¹)",
     ylab = "Predicted Flux",
     main = "Observed vs Predicted (RF, log-transformed 80/20 Model)",
     pch = 16, col = "darkgreen")
abline(0, 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)
```

```{r}
# ================================================================
```
```{r}
# ---- STEP 16: Residual Analysis and Mapping (Manual 80/20 RF Model) ----
# ================================================================

# Calculate residuals (Observed - Predicted)
test_data_log$pred_flux <- pred_flux_log
test_data_log$actual_flux <- actual_flux_log
test_data_log$residual <- test_data_log$actual_flux - test_data_log$pred_flux

# ---- Plot Residuals vs Predicted ----
plot(test_data_log$pred_flux, test_data_log$residual,
     xlab = "Predicted Flux (µmol m⁻² d⁻¹)",
     ylab = "Residual (Observed - Predicted)",
     main = "Residuals vs Predicted (Manual 80/20 RF, log-transformed)",
     pch = 16, col = "darkred")
abline(h = 0, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

# ---- Create Spatial Object for Mapping ----
residual_map_sf <- st_as_sf(
  test_data_log,
  coords = c("lon", "lat"),
  crs = 4326
)

# ---- Get World Basemap ----
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

# ---- Determine symmetric color scale ----
max_resid <- max(abs(test_data_log$residual), na.rm = TRUE)

# ---- Plot Spatial Distribution of Residuals ----
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = world, fill = "grey95", color = "grey70") +  # Land background
  geom_sf(data = residual_map_sf, aes(color = residual), size = 1) +
  scale_color_gradient2(
    low = "blue", mid = "grey", high = "red",
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "Residual\n(Observed - Predicted)"
  ) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-40, 40), ylim = c(20, 75), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Spatial Distribution of N₂O Flux Residuals (Manual 80/20 RF)",
    subtitle = "Europe and Surrounding Seas (Blue = Overprediction, Red = Underprediction)"
  )
```

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- # 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------- # 
# ---- STEP A: Comparing to Yang et al., 2020's Predicted N2O Flux
# ---- STEP A1: Loading and Extracting Yang et al.,2020's Predicted Flux ----
# --- Load Yang et al. (2020) dataset properly as SpatRaster ---
# --- 1. Load Yang et al. (2020) ensemble flux (SpatRaster) ---
yang_file <- "n2oFlux-Yang2020.nc"

# Load ensemble mean (use terra::rast to avoid class mismatch)
yang_flux_raster <- rast(yang_file, subds = "n2oFlux_EnsMean_g-pm2-pyr")

# --- 2. Convert units: g N₂O m⁻² yr⁻¹ → µmol N₂O m⁻² d⁻¹ ---
# (1 g N₂O = (1 / 44) mol = (1e6 / 44) µmol; divide by 365 for daily)
yang_flux_raster_umol <- yang_flux_raster * (1e6 / 44) / 365

# Some NetCDFs contain multiple layers (e.g., monthly). Collapse to mean.
yang_flux_umol_mean <- mean(yang_flux_raster_umol, na.rm = TRUE)
names(yang_flux_umol_mean) <- "Yang_Flux_umol"

# Optional: quick check
print(yang_flux_umol_mean)
summary(values(yang_flux_umol_mean))

# --- 3. Prepare coordinate data for extraction ---
# Add lat/lon from df_points if not already present
model_data_extended$lat <- df_points$lat[seq_len(nrow(model_data_extended))]
model_data_extended$lon <- df_points$lon[seq_len(nrow(model_data_extended))]

# Remove missing coordinates
model_data_extended <- model_data_extended %>% filter(!is.na(lat) & !is.na(lon))

# Convert to SpatVector for terra::extract
coords_vect <- vect(model_data_extended, geom = c("lon", "lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")

# --- 4. Extract Yang flux values at observation points ---
model_data_extended$flux_yang <- terra::extract(yang_flux_umol_mean, coords_vect)[, 1]

# --- 5. Predict N₂O fluxes using final 10-fold Random Forest model ---
pred_flux_final <- exp(predict(rf_final, newdata = model_data_extended))

# --- 6. Compute correlation ---
ok <- complete.cases(pred_flux_final, model_data_extended$flux_yang)
cor_rf_yang_final <- cor(pred_flux_final[ok], model_data_extended$flux_yang[ok])
cat("Correlation between 10-fold RF predictions and Yang et al. (2020):",
    round(cor_rf_yang_final, 3), "\n")

# --- 7. Visualize comparison ---
ggplot(model_data_extended[ok, ], aes(x = pred_flux_final[ok], y = flux_yang)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "darkred") +
  labs(
    title = "This Study's 10-fold RF Predictions vs Yang et al. (2020)",
    x = expression("This Study Predicted N"[2]*"O Flux (µmol m"^{-2}*" d"^{-1}*")"),
    y = expression("Yang et al. (2020) Predicted N"[2]*"O Flux (µmol m"^{-2}*" d"^{-1}*")")
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r}
# ---- STEP B: Include Yang et al. (2020) Flux as Predictor ----
cat("\n===== STEP B: Including Yang et al. (2020) Flux =====\n")

# Ensure Yang flux is extracted correctly
if (!"flux_yang" %in% names(df_points)) {
  cat("Extracting Yang et al. (2020) flux...\n")
  
  yang_file <- "n2oFlux-Yang2020.nc"
  yang_flux_raster <- raster(yang_file, varname = "n2oFlux_EnsMean_g-pm2-pyr")  # Ensemble mean

  # Convert from g N m⁻² yr⁻¹ → µmol N₂O m⁻² d⁻¹
  yang_flux_raster_umol <- yang_flux_raster * (1e6 / 44) / 365
  
  coords_sf <- st_as_sf(df_points, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
  df_points$flux_yang <- raster::extract(yang_flux_raster_umol, coords_sf)
  
  cat("Extraction complete.\n")
} else {
  cat("Yang flux already present.\n")
}

# Check for completeness
summary(df_points$flux_yang)

# Remove rows with missing data
df_points <- df_points %>% filter(complete.cases(.))

# ---- Define predictors including Yang flux ----
predictors_with_yang <- c("temperature", "salinity", "oxygen", "nitrate", 
                          "phosphate", "chlorophyll", "density", "depth", 
                          "lat", "lon", "flux_yang")

# Prepare modeling dataset
df_model_with_yang <- df_points %>%
  mutate(log_flux = log(flux + 1e-3)) %>%
  dplyr::select(log_flux, dplyr::all_of(predictors_with_yang)) %>%
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.)))

# Split into training/testing
set.seed(123)
train_idx_yang <- sample(seq_len(nrow(df_model_with_yang)), size = 0.8 * nrow(df_model_with_yang))
train_yang <- df_model_with_yang[train_idx_yang, ]
test_yang  <- df_model_with_yang[-train_idx_yang, ]

# ---- Train Random Forest including Yang flux ----
rf_yang_model <- randomForest(
  log_flux ~ ., 
  data = train_yang, 
  ntree = 500, 
  importance = TRUE
)

# ---- Evaluate performance ----
pred_log_flux_yang <- predict(rf_yang_model, newdata = test_yang)
pred_flux_yang <- exp(pred_log_flux_yang)
actual_flux_yang <- exp(test_yang$log_flux)

r2_yang <- cor(pred_flux_yang, actual_flux_yang)^2
rmse_yang <- sqrt(mean((pred_flux_yang - actual_flux_yang)^2))
mae_yang <- mean(abs(pred_flux_yang - actual_flux_yang))

cat("\n===== Enhanced Model with Yang Flux =====\n")
cat("Test R²:", round(r2_yang, 3), "\n")
cat("Test RMSE:", round(rmse_yang, 3), "\n")
cat("Test MAE:", round(mae_yang, 3), "\n")

# ---- Variable Importance ----
varImpPlot(rf_yang_model, main = "Variable Importance (RF + Yang Flux)")

# ---- Observed vs Predicted ----
plot(actual_flux_yang, pred_flux_yang,
     xlab = "Observed Flux (µmol m⁻² d⁻¹)",
     ylab = "Predicted Flux (µmol m⁻² d⁻¹)",
     main = "Observed vs Predicted (RF + Yang Flux)",
     pch = 16, col = "darkblue")
abline(0, 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)



# ---- FIXED & VERIFIED: Extract Yang et al. (2020) N₂O flux ----
cat("\n===== STEP: Extracting Yang et al. (2020) Flux =====\n")

# Load raster and ensure correct variable name
yang_file <- "n2oFlux-Yang2020.nc"
yang_flux_raster <- raster(yang_file, varname = "n2oFlux_EnsMean_g-pm2-pyr")

# Convert units: g N₂O m⁻² yr⁻¹ → µmol N₂O m⁻² d⁻¹
yang_flux_raster_umol <- yang_flux_raster * (1e6 / 44) / 365
names(yang_flux_raster_umol) <- "flux_yang"

# Force CRS consistency
crs(yang_flux_raster_umol) <- "EPSG:4326"
coords_sf <- st_as_sf(df_points, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)

# Extract flux values
cat("Extracting values from Yang raster...\n")
df_points$flux_yang <- raster::extract(yang_flux_raster_umol, coords_sf)

# Check success
if (!"flux_yang" %in% names(df_points)) {
  stop("Extraction failed: flux_yang not found in df_points")
}

na_rate <- mean(is.na(df_points$flux_yang))
if (na_rate > 0.5) {
  cat("⚠️ Warning: More than 50% NA values detected in flux_yang. Check coordinate alignment or raster extent.\n")
} else {
  cat("Extraction successful. Missing values:", round(na_rate * 100, 1), "%\n")
}

# Preview values
summary(df_points$flux_yang)
```

```{r}
# ---- STEP C: Add Biome Classification from Yang et al.,2020 ----
# ---- STEP C1: Load Yang’s Biome Raster and Extract Biome Labels
# Load Yang et al. biome raster from NetCDF
yang_file <- "dn2o-mapped-Yang2020.nc"

# Extract biome classification (1 to 6 as per their legend)
biome_raster <- raster(yang_file, varname = "biomes_masks")

# Extract biome category at your observation points
coords_sf_biome <- st_as_sf(df_points, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
df_points$biome <- raster::extract(biome_raster, coords_sf_biome)

# Convert biome to factor
df_points$biome <- factor(df_points$biome,
                          levels = 1:6,
                          labels = c("Tropical", "Upwelling", "Polar", "Mid-lat", "DeepMix", "SubtropicalGyre"))


# ---- STEP C2: Add Biome to Model and Train Again
# Add biome to your list of predictors
predictors_biome <- c(predictors_with_yang, "biome")  # All previous predictors + biome

# Filter complete cases
df_model_biome <- df_points %>%
  dplyr::select(log_flux, dplyr::all_of(predictors_biome)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.)))

# Split
set.seed(123)
train_idx_biome <- sample(seq_len(nrow(df_model_biome)), size = 0.8 * nrow(df_model_biome))
train_biome <- df_model_biome[train_idx_biome, ]
test_biome  <- df_model_biome[-train_idx_biome, ]

# Train model
rf_model_biome <- randomForest(log_flux ~ ., data = train_biome, ntree = 500, importance = TRUE)

# Evaluate
pred_biome_log <- predict(rf_model_biome, newdata = test_biome)
pred_biome <- exp(pred_biome_log)
actual_biome <- exp(test_biome$log_flux)

cat("\n===== Model with Biome Included =====\n")
cat("Test R²:", round(cor(pred_biome, actual_biome)^2, 3), "\n")
cat("Test RMSE:", round(sqrt(mean((pred_biome - actual_biome)^2)), 3), "\n")

# Optional: Variable importance
varImpPlot(rf_model_biome, main = "RF Variable Importance (Biome Included)")
```

```{r}
# ---- STEP E: Making Gridded Predictions ----
# ---- STEP E1: Stack Gridded Predictors into a Raster Brick
# 1. Load raw raster layers (keep only surface = depth 0)
temperature_r <- rast("woa2023_Temperature.nc", subds = "t_an")
temperature_r <- temperature_r[[grep("depth=0", names(temperature_r))]]

salinity_r <- rast("woa2023_Salinity.nc", subds = "s_an")
salinity_r <- salinity_r[[grep("depth=0", names(salinity_r))]]

oxygen_r <- rast("woa2023_DisOxygen.nc", subds = "o_an")
oxygen_r <- oxygen_r[[grep("depth=0", names(oxygen_r))]]

nitrate_r <- rast("woa2023_Nitrate.nc", subds = "n_an")
nitrate_r <- nitrate_r[[grep("depth=0", names(nitrate_r))]]

phosphate_r <- rast("woa2023_Phosphate.nc", subds = "p_an")
phosphate_r <- phosphate_r[[grep("depth=0", names(phosphate_r))]]

density_r <- rast("woa2018_Density.nc", subds = "I_an")
density_r <- density_r[[grep("depth=0", names(density_r))]]

depth_r <- rast("GEBCO_2025_sub_ice.nc")  # already 1 layer

# 2. Load and average chlorophyll (already surface-only)
chl_file1 <- "cmems_mod_glo_bgc_my_0.25deg_P1M-m_1760291720536.nc"
chl_file2 <- "cmems_mod_glo_bgc_myint_0.25deg_P1M-m_1760291822771.nc"

r1 <- rast(chl_file1)
r2 <- rast(chl_file2)

surface_names_r1 <- grep("chl_depth=0.50576", names(r1), value = TRUE)
surface_names_r2 <- grep("chl_depth=0.50576", names(r2), value = TRUE)

chl_stack1 <- r1[[surface_names_r1]]
chl_stack2 <- r2[[surface_names_r2]]

chl_full_stack <- c(chl_stack1, chl_stack2)
chlorophyll_r <- mean(chl_full_stack, na.rm = TRUE)

# 3. Crop to European extent
extent_europe <- ext(-35, 50, 20, 80)
rasters_uncropped <- list(
  temperature_r, salinity_r, oxygen_r, nitrate_r,
  phosphate_r, chlorophyll_r, density_r, depth_r
)
raster_list_cropped <- lapply(rasters_uncropped, function(r) crop(r, extent_europe))

# 4. Align CRS
for (i in seq_along(raster_list_cropped)) {
  crs(raster_list_cropped[[i]]) <- "EPSG:4326"
}

# 5. Align grids
ref_raster <- raster_list_cropped[[1]]
raster_list_aligned <- lapply(raster_list_cropped, function(r)
  resample(r, ref_raster, method = "bilinear")
)

# 6. Stack aligned rasters
predictor_stack <- rast(raster_list_aligned)
names(predictor_stack) <- c("temperature", "salinity", "oxygen", "nitrate",
                            "phosphate", "chlorophyll", "density", "depth")

# 7. Check
predictor_stack
plot(predictor_stack)


# ---- STEP E2: Predict N₂O Flux Across Europe Using RF Model ----
# Add Latitude and Longitude as Raster Layers ---
# --- Rebuild latitude and longitude rasters correctly ---
# Each one should have ONE layer only, aligned to the predictor grid
lat_raster <- rast(predictor_stack[[1]])  # copy geometry
lon_raster <- rast(predictor_stack[[1]])

# Fill with coordinate values
lat_raster[] <- yFromCell(lat_raster, 1:ncell(lat_raster))
lon_raster[] <- xFromCell(lon_raster, 1:ncell(lon_raster))

# Check that they’re single-layer rasters
nlyr(lat_raster)
nlyr(lon_raster)  

# Combine everything
predictor_stack_full <- c(predictor_stack, lat_raster, lon_raster)

# Verify number of layers (should be 10)
nlyr(predictor_stack_full)

names(predictor_stack_full) <- c("temperature", "salinity", "oxygen", "nitrate",
                                 "phosphate", "chlorophyll", "density", "depth",
                                 "lat", "lon")

# Predict log-fluxes using the final 10-fold cross-validated model
predicted_log_flux <- terra::predict(
  object   = predictor_stack_full,
  model    = rf_final,
  na.rm    = TRUE,
  progress = TRUE
)

# Back-transform to µmol N₂O m⁻² d⁻¹
predicted_flux <- exp(predicted_log_flux)
names(predicted_flux) <- "Predicted_N2O_Flux"

# Save and visualize
writeRaster(predicted_flux, "Predicted_N2O_Flux_Europe_RFfinal.tif", overwrite = TRUE)

plot(predicted_flux, col = viridis::viridis(100),
     main = expression("Predicted N"[2]*"O Flux (µmol m"^{-2}*" d"^{-1}*")"))

cat("Predicted flux mean:", round(global(predicted_flux, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]], 3), "\n")
cat("Predicted flux range:", round(global(predicted_flux, "min", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]], 3), "–",
    round(global(predicted_flux, "max", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]], 3), "\n")
```

```{r}
# ---- STEP 18: Train Basic XGBoost Model (Using predictors available for grid) ----
#  Define matching predictors (for both model and gridded stack)
predictors_basic <- c("lat", "lon", "temperature", "salinity", "oxygen", 
                      "nitrate", "phosphate", "chlorophyll", "density", "depth")

#  Prepare cleaned input data with only these predictors
xgb_data_basic <- df_points %>%
  mutate(log_flux = log(flux + 1e-3)) %>%  # re-define here if needed
  dplyr::select(log_flux, dplyr::all_of(predictors_basic)) %>%
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.)))

#  Extract predictor matrix and target vector
X_basic <- as.matrix(xgb_data_basic[, predictors_basic])  # predictor matrix
y_basic <- xgb_data_basic$log_flux                        # target vector

#  Add explicit column names to matrix BEFORE DMatrix
colnames(X_basic) <- predictors_basic

#  Train/test split
set.seed(42)
train_idx_basic <- sample(seq_len(nrow(X_basic)), size = 0.8 * nrow(X_basic))
X_train_basic <- X_basic[train_idx_basic, ]
y_train_basic <- y_basic[train_idx_basic]
X_test_basic  <- X_basic[-train_idx_basic, ]
y_test_basic  <- y_basic[-train_idx_basic]

#  DMatrix for XGBoost
dtrain_basic <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_train_basic, label = y_train_basic)
dtest_basic  <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_test_basic, label = y_test_basic)

#  Train basic XGBoost model
xgb_model_basic <- xgboost(
  data = dtrain_basic,
  nrounds = 200,
  objective = "reg:squarederror",
  eval_metric = "rmse",
  verbose = 0
)

#  Predict and evaluate
pred_log_basic <- predict(xgb_model_basic, newdata = dtest_basic)
pred_flux_basic <- exp(pred_log_basic)
actual_flux_basic <- exp(y_test_basic)

#  Evaluation metrics
r2_basic <- cor(pred_flux_basic, actual_flux_basic)^2
rmse_basic <- sqrt(mean((pred_flux_basic - actual_flux_basic)^2))
cat("Basic XGBoost Model R²:", round(r2_basic, 3), "\n")
cat("Basic XGBoost Model RMSE:", round(rmse_basic, 3), "\n")
```

```{r}
#  ---- XGBoost Model with 10-Fold Cross-Validation ----
# ================================================================

set.seed(42)

# Define matching predictors
predictors_basic <- c("lat", "lon", "temperature", "salinity", "oxygen",
                      "nitrate", "phosphate", "chlorophyll", "density", "depth")

# Prepare cleaned dataset
xgb_data_basic <- df_points %>%
  mutate(log_flux = log(flux + 1e-3)) %>%
  dplyr::select(log_flux, dplyr::all_of(predictors_basic)) %>%
  filter(if_all(everything(), ~ !is.na(.)))

# --------------------------
# Use caret::train for CV
# --------------------------
ctrl_xgb <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 10,          # 10-fold cross-validation
  verboseIter = TRUE,
  savePredictions = "final"
)

# Define hyperparameter grid 
xgb_grid <- expand.grid(
  nrounds = c(200, 300),
  max_depth = c(4, 6),
  eta = c(0.05, 0.1),
  gamma = 0,
  colsample_bytree = c(0.8),
  min_child_weight = 1,
  subsample = c(0.8)
)

# Train cross-validated XGBoost model
xgb_cv <- train(
  log_flux ~ .,
  data = xgb_data_basic,
  method = "xgbTree",
  trControl = ctrl_xgb,
  tuneGrid = xgb_grid,
  verbose = TRUE
)

print(xgb_cv)
plot(xgb_cv)

# Extract best hyperparameters
best_params <- xgb_cv$bestTune
cat("Best XGBoost parameters:\n")
print(best_params)

# Mean cross-validated performance
best_results <- xgb_cv$results[
  with(xgb_cv$results,
       nrounds == best_params$nrounds &
       max_depth == best_params$max_depth &
       eta == best_params$eta),
]
cat("10-fold CV mean R²:", round(best_results$Rsquared, 3), "\n")
cat("10-fold CV mean RMSE:", round(best_results$RMSE, 3), "\n")

# Retrain final model on full dataset with best parameters
final_xgb <- xgboost(
  data = xgb.DMatrix(as.matrix(xgb_data_basic[, predictors_basic]),
                     label = xgb_data_basic$log_flux),
  nrounds = best_params$nrounds,
  max_depth = best_params$max_depth,
  eta = best_params$eta,
  subsample = best_params$subsample,
  colsample_bytree = best_params$colsample_bytree,
  objective = "reg:squarederror",
  eval_metric = "rmse",
  verbose = 0
)

saveRDS(final_xgb, "xgb_final_model.rds")
```

```{r}
# -------------------------------------------
# Scenario Analysis: N₂O Flux Sensitivity
# Based on predictor_stack and XGBoost tuned model
# -------------------------------------------
# Clone base stack
stack_base <- predictor_stack

# Define scenario modifications
stack_temp2C <- stack_base
stack_temp2C[["temperature"]] <- stack_temp2C[["temperature"]] + 2

stack_oxygen20 <- stack_base
stack_oxygen20[["oxygen"]] <- stack_oxygen20[["oxygen"]] * 0.8

stack_nutrient20 <- stack_base
stack_nutrient20[["nitrate"]] <- stack_nutrient20[["nitrate"]] * 1.2
stack_nutrient20[["phosphate"]] <- stack_nutrient20[["phosphate"]] * 1.2

stack_multi <- stack_base
stack_multi[["temperature"]] <- stack_multi[["temperature"]] + 2
stack_multi[["oxygen"]] <- stack_multi[["oxygen"]] * 0.8
stack_multi[["nitrate"]] <- stack_multi[["nitrate"]] * 1.2
stack_multi[["phosphate"]] <- stack_multi[["phosphate"]] * 1.2

# Convert
to_grid_df <- function(stack) {
  df <- as.data.frame(stack, xy = TRUE)
  df <- df[complete.cases(df), ]
  df
}

df_base <- to_grid_df(stack_base)
df_temp <- to_grid_df(stack_temp2C)
df_o2   <- to_grid_df(stack_oxygen20)
df_nut  <- to_grid_df(stack_nutrient20)
df_multi <- to_grid_df(stack_multi)

# --- CLEAN COLUMN NAMES ---
fix_coords <- function(df) {
  # Remove duplicate names
  df <- df[, !duplicated(names(df))]
  
  # Rename coordinate columns
  if ("x" %in% names(df)) names(df)[names(df) == "x"] <- "lon"
  if ("y" %in% names(df)) names(df)[names(df) == "y"] <- "lat"
  
  return(df)
}

df_base  <- fix_coords(df_base)
df_temp  <- fix_coords(df_temp)
df_o2    <- fix_coords(df_o2)
df_nut   <- fix_coords(df_nut)
df_multi <- fix_coords(df_multi)

predict_flux <- function(df, predictors, model) {
  mat <- as.matrix(df[, predictors])
  colnames(mat) <- predictors
  pred <- predict(model, newdata = mat)
  exp(pred)
}


# ---- Predict flux for each scenario using the final 10-fold model ----
predictors <- predictors_basic  # already defined earlier

df_base$flux  <- predict_flux(df_base,  predictors, final_xgb)
df_temp$flux  <- predict_flux(df_temp,  predictors, final_xgb)
df_o2$flux    <- predict_flux(df_o2,    predictors, final_xgb)
df_nut$flux   <- predict_flux(df_nut,   predictors, final_xgb)
df_multi$flux <- predict_flux(df_multi, predictors, final_xgb)

# Calculate deltas (flux difference from baseline)
df_temp$delta <- df_temp$flux - df_base$flux
df_o2$delta   <- df_o2$flux - df_base$flux
df_nut$delta  <- df_nut$flux - df_base$flux
df_multi$delta <- df_multi$flux - df_base$flux

# Visualize difference
plot_scenario <- function(df, title) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = delta)) +
    geom_raster() +
    geom_sf(data = land, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            fill = "gray90", color = "gray50", size = 0.1) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "blue", mid = "grey", high = "red", midpoint = 0,
      name = expression(Delta * "N"[2]*"O Flux (µmol m"^{-2}*" d"^{-1}*")")
    ) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(-30, 60), ylim = c(30, 75), expand = FALSE) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = title, x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))
}


plot_scenario <- function(df, title) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = delta)) +
    geom_raster() +
    geom_sf(data = land, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            fill = "gray90", color = "gray50", size = 0.1) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red",
      limits = c(-0.5, 0.5),        # ADD A LIMIT
      oob = scales::squish,     
      midpoint = 0,
      name = expression(Delta * "N"[2]*"O Flux (µmol m"^{-2}*" d"^{-1}*")")
    ) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(-30, 60), ylim = c(30, 75), expand = FALSE) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = title, x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right"
    )
}

plot_scenario(df_temp,  "a) Scenario: +2°C Temperature")
 plot_scenario(df_o2,    "b) Scenario: -20% Oxygen")
 plot_scenario(df_nut,   "c) Scenario: +20% Nutrients")
 plot_scenario(df_multi, "d) Scenario: Combined Drivers")

 # ---- Quantify Scenario Magnitudes ----
# Function to summarize flux changes
summarize_scenario <- function(df, name) {
  baseline_mean <- mean(df_base$flux, na.rm = TRUE)
  delta_mean <- mean(df$delta, na.rm = TRUE)
  delta_median <- median(df$delta, na.rm = TRUE)
  percent_change <- (mean(df$flux, na.rm = TRUE) - baseline_mean) / baseline_mean * 100
  data.frame(
    Scenario = name,
    Mean_Delta = delta_mean,
    Median_Delta = delta_median,
    Percent_Change = percent_change
  )
}

scen_stats <- rbind(
  summarize_scenario(df_temp, "Warming (+2°C)"),
  summarize_scenario(df_o2,   "Deoxygenation (−20% O₂)"),
  summarize_scenario(df_nut,  "Nutrient enrichment (+20%)"),
  summarize_scenario(df_multi,"Combined drivers")
)

print(scen_stats)
```

```{r}
# =============================================================
# ---- Model Uncertainty: Bootstrap Random Forests (10-fold RF) ----
# =============================================================

# Parameters
n_bootstrap <- 100   
set.seed(42)

# ---- Ensure lat/lon layers exist ----
lat_raster <- rast(predictor_stack[[1]])
lon_raster <- rast(predictor_stack[[1]])
lat_raster[] <- yFromCell(lat_raster, 1:ncell(lat_raster))
lon_raster[] <- xFromCell(lon_raster, 1:ncell(lon_raster))

predictor_stack_full <- c(predictor_stack, lat_raster, lon_raster)
names(predictor_stack_full) <- c(
  "temperature", "salinity", "oxygen", "nitrate", "phosphate",
  "chlorophyll", "density", "depth", "lat", "lon"
)

# ---- Prepare clean dataset for bootstrapping ----
predictor_vars <- c("temperature", "salinity", "oxygen", "nitrate",
                    "phosphate", "chlorophyll", "density", "depth", "lat", "lon")

# Keep only predictors + target variable
model_data_boot <- model_data_extended %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(c("log_flux", predictor_vars))) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.))

# ---- Initialize storage for bootstrap results ----
bootstrap_rasters <- list()

# ---- Display progress bar (helps me to keep track how long it might take ----
pb <- txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = n_bootstrap, style = 3)

# ---- Bootstrap loop ----
for (i in 1:n_bootstrap) {
  cat("\nTraining bootstrap model:", i, "\n")
  
  # Sample with replacement
  boot_idx <- sample(nrow(model_data_boot), replace = TRUE)
  boot_data <- model_data_boot[boot_idx, ]
  
  # Remove any remaining NAs just in case
  boot_data <- boot_data %>% filter(complete.cases(.))
  if (nrow(boot_data) == 0) next  # skip if empty
  
  # Train bootstrap Random Forest
  rf_boot <- randomForest(
    log_flux ~ .,
    data = boot_data,
    ntree = 500,
    mtry = rf_final$mtry
  )
  
  # Predict over gridded stack
  pred_log_boot <- terra::predict(
    predictor_stack_full,
    rf_boot,
    na.rm = TRUE,
    progress = FALSE
  )
  
  # Back-transform (log → natural scale)
  flux_boot <- exp(pred_log_boot)
  
  # Store raster
  bootstrap_rasters[[i]] <- flux_boot
  
  # Update progress bar
  setTxtProgressBar(pb, i)
}

close(pb)

# ---- Combine bootstrap rasters ----
bootstrap_stack <- rast(bootstrap_rasters)

# ---- Compute mean and standard deviation ----
flux_mean <- mean(bootstrap_stack, na.rm = TRUE)
flux_sd   <- app(bootstrap_stack, fun = sd, na.rm = TRUE)

# ---- Plot results ----
plot(flux_mean, main = "Bootstrap Mean N₂O Flux",
     col = viridis::viridis(100))
plot(flux_sd, main = "Prediction Uncertainty (SD)",
     col = viridis::magma(100))

# ---- Convert to dataframe for ggplot ----
uncertainty_df <- as.data.frame(flux_sd, xy = TRUE)
names(uncertainty_df)[3] <- "uncertainty"
uncertainty_df <- na.omit(uncertainty_df)

# ---- Load land polygons ----
land <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")

# ---- ggplot visualization ----
ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = uncertainty_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = uncertainty)) +
  geom_sf(data = land, fill = "gray90", color = "gray50", size = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_viridis(
    name = expression("Prediction SD (µmol m"^{-2}*" d"^{-1}*")"),
    option = "C"
  ) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-30, 60), ylim = c(30, 75), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Prediction Uncertainty (Bootstrap SD)",
    x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```

```{r}
# 1) Choose predictors (same as RF “core 8”)
predictor_vars <- c("temperature","salinity","oxygen","nitrate",
                    "phosphate","chlorophyll","density","depth")

# 2) Build clean matrix from your point table
env_df <- df_points %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(c("lat","lon", predictor_vars))) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(.))

# Diagnostics: zero-variance columns (kill them)
zv <- sapply(env_df[, predictor_vars, drop = FALSE], function(x) var(x, na.rm = TRUE) == 0)
if (any(zv)) {
  message("Removed zero-variance predictors: ", paste(names(zv)[zv], collapse=", "))
  predictor_vars <- predictor_vars[!zv]
}
if (length(predictor_vars) < 2) {
  stop("Not enough varying predictors to cluster. Aborting clustering.")
}

# 3) Keep only predictors and de-duplicate identical environments
X <- env_df[, predictor_vars, drop = FALSE]
X_unique <- X %>% distinct()
n_unique <- nrow(X_unique)
message("Unique environmental rows: ", n_unique)

if (n_unique < 2) {
  stop("All rows are identical after cleaning; clustering is not feasible.")
}

# 4) Scale and choose a feasible k automatically
Xu_scaled <- scale(X_unique)
k <- max(2, min(4, n_unique - 1))
message("Using k = ", k, " (auto-selected).")

# 5) Run k-means on UNIQUE environments
set.seed(42)
km <- kmeans(Xu_scaled, centers = k, nstart = 50)

# 6) Map cluster labels back to ALL rows
#    Do exact matching on raw (unscaled) unique rows
#    (Use a key made from rounded values to avoid floating-point noise)
key_fun <- function(df) apply(round(as.matrix(df), 6), 1, paste, collapse = "|")
key_unique <- key_fun(X_unique)
key_all    <- key_fun(X)

# lookup table: unique-row key -> cluster id
lut <- setNames(km$cluster, key_unique)

# attach cluster to env_df
env_df$cluster <- factor(lut[key_all], levels = 1:k,
                         labels = paste0("Cluster ", 1:k))

# 7) Quick summaries
print(table(env_df$cluster))
cluster_centers <- as.data.frame(scale(X_unique) %*% diag(0, ncol(X_unique)))
# (optional) show scaled centers with names:
centers_df <- as.data.frame(km$centers)
centers_df$cluster <- paste0("Cluster ", 1:k)
centers_df <- centers_df[, c(ncol(centers_df), 1:(ncol(centers_df)-1))]
print(centers_df)

# 8) Map (only if there are positions for these rows)
try({
  world <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
  pts_sf <- st_as_sf(env_df, coords = c("lon","lat"), crs = 4326)
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = world, fill = "gray95", color = "gray70") +
    geom_sf(data = pts_sf, aes(color = cluster), alpha = 0.85, size = 1.2) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(-30, 60), ylim = c(30, 75), expand = FALSE) +
    scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
    labs(title = paste0("Environmental Clusters (k = ", k, ")"),
         x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude", color = "Cluster") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))
}, silent = TRUE)

# 9) Optional: PCA cluster plot (on the unique environments)
try({
  fviz_cluster(km, data = Xu_scaled,
               geom = "point", ellipse.type = "norm",
               main = paste("K-means on Unique Environments (k =", k, ")"))
}, silent = TRUE)
```
